cards.name: Markov expected-run engine
cards.role: Optimization currency and same-nine ordering evaluation
inputs: Player PA outcome probabilities (neutral / vs RHP / vs LHP)
limitations: Does not model mid-game substitutions or intentional walks as decisions
Single-game observed runs are high-variance; validate on aggregates
cards.validation: See markov_validation.json (out-of-time predicted vs actual R/G)

cards.name: Same-nine batting-order optimizer
cards.role: Exhaustive ranking of 9! orders for fixed personnel
inputs: PA probability matrix for a platoon context
limitations: Percentile can look dramatic when thousands of orders are nearly equivalent
Fast exhaustive scores are refined with full Markov evaluations at endpoints
cards.validation: Correlation checks between fast ranks and full-engine ranks in tests

cards.name: PA outcome probability store
cards.role: Batter talent / platoon skill inputs to the Markov engine
inputs: Historical plate appearances with outcome classes
outputs: 7-class outcome probabilities per player and context
limitations: Small-sample players shrink toward league averages
Does not encode park or pitcher identity beyond hand splits

cards.name: Residual interaction / chemistry models
cards.role: Test whether adjacent-hitter identity improves prediction after talent/state controls
inputs: Adjacent PA frame with previous batter, state, pitcher hand
outputs: Out-of-sample log-loss / RMSE lift vs baseline models
limitations: One temporal split is insufficient; prefer multi-fold rolling validation

cards.name: Exploratory offensive profile groups
cards.role: Descriptive clustering of hitter skill profiles
limitations: Low silhouette implies weak natural separation
Treat as exploratory unless assignment stability is validated

notes: Expected runs remain the optimization currency for same-nine comparisons.
Cross-team ranking should prioritize ordering gaps and near-optimal rates over raw expected runs.
